newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Thousands cross to Angola from Zaire - aid workers.
newsitem.headline: Thousands cross to Angola from Zaire - aid workers.

text.p: Thousands of people, including armed men, have crossed the border from Zaire into parts of north Angola controlled by the former rebel movement UNITA, local residents, officials and aid workers said on Thursday.
"Apparently some 25,000 Hutus have crossed into UNITA-held areas in the Lundas (region in the north-east) from Zaire," said one official close to Angola's peace process who declined to be named.
Government and military authorities were not available for comment.
The official said many of the estimated 25,000 were from Rwanda's Hutu-led former army and their militia allies or UNITA soldiers returning from Zaire.

Angola's government accuses UNITA of sending some 15,000 troops to help shore up the rule of former president Mobutu Sese Seko, who fled a week ago and was replaced as head of state by rebel leader Laurent Kabila.

Residents near the city of Maquela do Zombo in north Angola also reported a large influx of people. They said by telephone that they had seen armed men and apparently wealthy civilians from Zaire passing by the city.
